title: Up to the castle
steps: The castle's great door stands open at last, the last seal broken.
We did it! We opened it together!

Just think of the first step to the gate, the fixed note, and the long walk in one instruction! A program is a list of instructions; your wizard is an object, the one the code calls `wizard`, and its actions are methods; a comment is a note for a person, and a move's argument says how far.

Then came the password *ambrel*, the wand, and breaking the seals with *zelim*. A string is words in quotes, kept exactly as written, and `say` says one; `pick_up` picks a thing up, and a spell is cast with the wand.
Thank you for teaching me, {friend}. I think using the wand was my favorite part!

The wand is only lent! Our teacher, Ilda, waits inside, and the wand bank, a counter in the castle run by the pupils' parents, lends every new pupil a school wand for the year; then you can give my spare back.
Together you step into the castle; the real castle begins.
